notes:
Summary: Mid-market product analytics SaaS evaluating Redwood Hosted API as a fast path, moving toward Dedicated once throughput and cost baselines are locked. Customer team: Head of Product (Ana Ruiz), Platform Eng (Michael Torre), CTO (Samir Patel). Trial timeline:

Recent timeline / activity:
- 2025-11-05: Initial discovery (AE Evan Morales). High-level fit: chat + embeddings + rerank for in-app help and search relevance.
- 2026-01-12: Hosted API sign-up, sandbox integration using SDK.
- 2026-02-24: 60-minute technical review (Fireflies: ff_2026-02-24_789234). Covered auth, data flows, and latency targets.
- 2026-03-02: POC wrap-up call (Fireflies: ff_2026-03-02_812345). Shared hosted trial metrics and asked for Dedicated sizing.
- 2026-03-05: Pricing email thread started (thread-Gm_2026-03-05-483).

Hosted API trial findings (observed):
- Average QPS (requests/sec): ~6 sustained during weekday peak windows (2pm-4pm PT).
- Peak concurrent requests observed: ~120 simultaneous in-app chat widgets (spiky traffic during product release).
- Token mix (observed distribution): 65% short prompts (<=128 tokens), 30% medium (128-512 tokens), 5% long/context retrieval (>1024 tokens).
- Average output tokens per request: ~220 tokens. Estimated monthly tokens during trial: ~45M; projected production baseline: 1.5B tokens/mo at 3x current usage within 6 months.
- Latency target: P50 < 250ms for short prompts, P95 < 800ms overall (they accept slightly higher P95 for long context replies).
- Cost sensitivity: high — product team targets cost/unit token that keeps feature monetizable for freemium users.

Dedicated sizing assumptions and asks from customer:
- Baseline QPS target for Dedicated sizing: 35 QPS sustained with burst headroom to 120 QPS for release days.
- Concurrency model: want to reserve for 150 concurrent sessions to avoid tail latency during spikes.
- KV/prefix caching expected for ~40% of requests (search rerank + common help prompts).
- Preferred model family: open LLM variants verified by Redwood (4k/8k context models); willing to consider quantized variants for cost.
- Required SLAs: 99.9% uptime, region routing to NA, private VPC peering for data egress.

POC requests completed / deliverables asked: 
- Redwood to deliver a Dedicated capacity worksheet (QPS -> GPU pool sizing -> monthly cost) with multiple options: conservative/expected/aggressive.
- Demo of canary fallback (hosted -> dedicated fallback) and routing policy examples.
- Security questionnaire answers (completed) and timeline for SOC2 evidence. Docs: drive:/Redwood/pricing/rivermount_dedicated_pricing_v2.pdf.

Customer quotes / notes from calls:
- "We need predictable unit costs and a straightforward path to reserved capacity — if the math works we can commit." — Ana Ruiz, Head of Product.
- "Peak concurrency assumptions will make or break this deal; we need the Dedicated sizing to show headroom without 3x cost blowup." — Michael Torre, Platform Eng.

Next steps (short):
- Redwood ACTION: send Dedicated capacity worksheet + 3-tier pricing and expected throughput mapping (ETA 2026-03-11).
- Customer ACTION: internal infra/finance sync scheduled 2026-03-18 to review pricing and procurement path.
- Follow-up scheduled: 2026-03-20 technical Q&A + legal DPA draft.

Open blockers: budget approval, legal (DPA + data residency terms), final SOC2 evidence for procurement, confirm long-term model selection (quantized vs full precision).

Internal notes for AE/SE: assume mid-market contract with 12mo commitment if pricing meets cost per token threshold. Prioritize sizing scenarios that show cost savings via batching/prefix caching. Attach POC workbook (drive:/Redwood/POCs/rivermount_poc_results_2026-03.xlsx).
